frequency_question: How often do joint resolutions of disapproval successfully pass both chambers and survive or override an executive veto to block a major executive-level international agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal congressional review actions under the AEA or AECA targeting major bilateral nuclear or arms agreements since the 1976 Nelson-Bingham Amendment and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act of 1978. Excludes informal expressions of concern or non-binding resolutions.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named historical high-salience statutory disapproval attempts; believed to be exhaustive for major executive-level defense/nuclear pacts facing formal congressional disapproval votes.
known_gaps: Lower-salience or committee-level actions that did not reach full floor votes under identical procedures are excluded, but these would lower the success rate further if included.
skeleton: Legislative veto / joint resolution of disapproval attempts under statutory foreign policy review frameworks vs presidential veto power.
multiplier: 0 successful overrides or veto-proof blocks out of 5 major contested high-stakes congressional disapproval votes on similar foreign/nuclear pacts.
validity_reason: The structural constitutional friction between Congress and the Executive regarding treaty and agreement veto overrides remains governed by Article I Section 7 and specific statutory frameworks established in the 1970s, which remain stable.
